magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on parents responding with tenderness, closeness, and redirection of attention can be in harmony with Christian care for the child, and Church guidelines indeed call for a gentle and prudent approach to early bodily habits. However, the claim that childhood genital stimulation is primarily a substitute for a lack of tenderness is not established in the attached Church sources and may overly simplify the causes of the behavior.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic approach holds together tender parental care and education in chastity: parents can redirect the child's attention and offer closeness, while calmly teaching modesty and an appropriate attitude toward the body. Church guidelines also warn that education must seek the causes of difficulties, and not merely directly suppress their occurrence, and if necessary involve professionally trained persons.
concerns_en: The explanation that the child satisfies the need for tenderness through such behavior is presented as a causal claim, but the attached guidelines do not confirm that a lack of tenderness is a general or primary explanation; they recommend a prudent determination of possible causes and, when necessary, consultation with qualified professionals.

The term "child stimulation" can usefully distinguish the behavior of a small child from the conscious, morally responsible act of an adult, but it should not serve to deny that it is genital behavior that parents can gently guide. Church guidelines speak of early genital behavior and recommend gentle correction of habits that could later develop into sinful habits.

The passage does not elaborate on the distinction between the child's behavior itself and its personal moral guilt. Guidelines prescribe gentle correction within a positive framework of dignity, rather than shaming or an automatic attribution of full moral responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: From the need for tenderness to the latency phase: what parents need to know about early phases
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the early childhood phase, the need for tenderness, and the latency phase
sections.content_en:
While the child is small, says Josipa Nemet, such an example of the parents is sufficient and nothing else is needed. A small child satisfies its needs to a great extent through **touch and tenderness**. If tenderness is lacking, the child can seek it on its own, by stimulating parts of the body where it has nerve endings. Activists, she notes, call this masturbation. She describes it as **child stimulation** with which the child satisfies the need for tenderness.

The advice to parents is to **redirect** the child's attention, to pick it up, spend time with it, and cuddle it. Then the child "drinks its fill of the parents" and of that tenderness, so it naturally grows out of such behavior. At a certain age, it also instinctively understands on its own not to do this in front of others. It is crucial **not to attack the child** and not to give it the impression that something is wrong with its body, because it feels only pleasure. It is a frequent mistake, she says, that parents are shocked then, even though it is a completely normal stage.

Next comes the **latency phase**, in which interest in that bodily pleasure is lost. That is, she points out, a very important period of preadolescence. The child naturally turns outward: toward the community, learning, and gaining experience. In the brain, a "huge synaptic explosion" takes place, so the child is like a **sponge for culture**. Then parents can slowly pass on the basics to it.

It is best, she advises, to wait for the child to ask questions on its own. Whether it will ask them depends on whether it has a close relationship with the parent and whether the topic is stigmatized. Answers must be adapted to age. Parents can also educate themselves from "wonderful books" about talking to children about sexuality, and the association, the guest adds, also organizes **workshops on how to talk to children about sexuality**.

sections.subtitle: Pubertet kao otkriće komplementarnosti i opasnost od devet minuta razgovora dnevno
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet upozorava na statistiku da roditelji s djecom razgovaraju svega 8 do 9 minuta
sections.content:
Kad se dijete približava spolnoj zrelosti, primjerice uz prvu menstruaciju, mora dobiti informacije o vlastitoj **fiziologiji**, objašnjava Josipa Nemet. Važno je, međutim, kako mu se te informacije prenose. Cilj je da se dijete, kako kaže, „zaljubi u to“, da vidi koliko je ljudsko tijelo lijepo i usklađeno.

To vrijedi i za djevojčice i za dječake. Usporedbom fizionomije dijete može uočiti **ljepotu komplementarnosti**: riječ je o jedinom sustavu koji je sam po sebi nedostatan, kojemu je potrebna druga osoba i koji svoju svrhu ostvaruje tek u zajedništvu s njom.

Iz toga gošća izvodi širu misao: **djeca se odgajaju kroz priče**, i kroz cijelu ljudsku povijest i danas. Djeca priče i traže. Problem je što se s njima više ne razgovara. Navodi „tragičnu statistiku“ prema kojoj roditelj s djetetom u prosjeku razgovara **8 do 9 minuta**, što naziva zastrašujućim. Bez narativa, priče i riječi, kaže, nema razvoja novog čovjeka.

Upozorenje je jasno: dijete će se, ako mu roditelji ne pričaju dobre priče, „ugraditi“ u **loše priče**. One ga fragmentiraju i neće ga izgraditi u odraslu osobu sposobnu stvarati nešto lijepo, živjeti za druge i doprinositi obitelji i zajednici.

magisterium.assessment: Pozitivno je što se pubertet i fiziologija prikazuju otvoreno i kao nešto lijepo, a spolna razlika i komplementarnost imaju uporište u biblijskom prikazu čovjeka kao muškog i ženskog te u katoličkom razumijevanju braka i rađanja života. Ipak, tvrdnja da je čovjekov spolni sustav „sam po sebi nedostatan“ traži pojašnjenje kako ne bi sugerirala da je svaka osoba nepotpuna bez partnera ili da se ljudska vrijednost svodi na reproduktivnu funkciju.
concerns: Izraz „jedini sustav koji je sam po sebi nedostatan“ može zvučati kao da se o čovjeku govori prvenstveno kao o reproduktivnom sustavu, a ne kao o osobi dostojanstva koje ne ovisi o plodnosti ili braku.
Komplementarnost muškarca i žene ne znači da svaki pojedinac mora biti u braku ili da bez bračnog partnera osobno nije cjelovit; odlomak tu važnu razliku ne izriče.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličke smjernice podupiru dobno primjerene i istinite informacije o pubertetu, dane mirno i pozitivno, u okviru čednosti, braka, obitelji i prokreacije; spolnost pritom nije nešto sramotno, nego Božji dar. Biblijski govor o „jednom tijelu“ upućuje na bračno zajedništvo koje poštuje osobitost obaju supružnika, dok crkveni nauk istodobno prepoznaje i životni poziv koji se ostvaruje drukčijim življenjem tjelesnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: It is positive that puberty and physiology are presented openly and as something beautiful, and sexual difference and complementarity are grounded in the biblical depiction of man as male and female and in the Catholic understanding of marriage and the procreation of life. Still, the claim that man's sexual system is „insufficient in itself“ requires clarification so as not to suggest that every person is incomplete without a partner or that human worth is reduced to reproductive function.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic guidelines support age-appropriate and truthful information about puberty, given calmly and positively, within the framework of chastity, marriage, family, and procreation; sexuality is not something shameful, but a gift of God. Biblical discourse on „one flesh“ points to marital communion that respects the distinctiveness of both spouses, while Church teaching simultaneously recognizes a vocation in life that is realized by living one's corporeality differently.
concerns_en: The phrase „the only system that is insufficient in itself“ may sound as though man is spoken of primarily as a reproductive system, rather than as a person of dignity that does not depend on fertility or marriage.

The complementarity of man and woman does not mean that every individual must be married or that without a marital partner one is not personally complete; the passage does not articulate this important distinction.

sections.subtitle_en: Puberty as a discovery of complementarity and the danger of nine minutes of conversation a day
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet warns of the statistic that parents talk with their children for only 8 to 9 minutes
sections.content_en:
When a child approaches sexual maturity, for example with the first menstruation, they must receive information about their own **physiology**, explains Josipa Nemet. It is important, however, how this information is conveyed to them. The goal is for the child, as she says, „to fall in love with it“, to see how beautiful and harmonious the human body is.

This applies to both girls and boys. By comparing physiognomy, a child can notice the **beauty of complementarity**: it is the only system that is insufficient in itself, which needs another person and which realizes its purpose only in communion with them.

From this, the guest derives a broader thought: **children are raised through stories**, both throughout all human history and today. Children also seek stories. The problem is that people no longer talk with them. She cites a „tragic statistic“ according to which a parent talks with a child on average **8 to 9 minutes**, which she calls terrifying. Without narrative, story, and words, she says, there is no development of a new human being.

The warning is clear: if parents do not tell them good stories, the child will „embed“ themselves into **bad stories**. They fragment them and will not build them into an adult person capable of creating something beautiful, living for others, and contributing to family and community.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: puna kuća djece, heklanje, stroga pravila i svetost kao mjera uspjeha
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja blic pitanja, a gošća odgovara uz osmijeh
sections.content:
Voditelj priznaje da mu je žao prekidati razgovor i da bi se moglo još dugo razgovarati. Prije kraja ipak postavlja nekoliko blic pitanja tipa „ili-ili“, unaprijed upozoravajući da su neka „škakljiva“. Odgovori Josipe Nemet otkrivaju njezinu osobnost:

- **Znanstveni laboratorij ili puna kuća djece?** Bez oklijevanja: puna kuća djece. Voditelj komentira da je to bilo „ziher“.
- **Košarkaška utakmica ili mirna večera uz knjigu?** Sada već mirna večera uz knjigu. Gleda li se utakmicu, ne voli gledati, nego igrati. Da je izbor bio između heklanja i knjige, vjerojatno bi izabrala heklanje.
- **Roditeljski sastanak ili TV sučeljavanje?** Roditeljski sastanak, jer više voli susret s ljudima uživo nego sve „bestjelesno“. Ondje, kaže, ima i dobrih prijatelja.
- **Homeschooling ili potpuna reforma školstva?** Za njezinu obitelj i karaktere njezine djece bolja je škola, i to dobre škole.
- **Znanstveni rad ili javni aktivizam?** Velika snaga žene je u utjecaju, a s obzirom na svoj karakter smatra da je za društvo plodnija u javnom aktivizmu.
- **Stroga pravila ili potpuno povjerenje u djecu?** Stroga pravila, uz napomenu da su djeca tako sretnija. Voditelj dodaje: kad znaju granice.
- **Rasprava s ideološkim protivnikom ili pet sati dječjih tantruma?** Ni jedno ni drugo, a objektivna ne može biti jer joj tantrum nikad nije trajao toliko dugo i za to ima „svoje metode“. Ipak voli raspravljati s ideološkim protivnicima, ali na lijep način: kao natjecanje u razmišljanju, a ne debatu u kojoj se drugoga ponižava. U takvom razgovoru, smatra, oboje rastu.
- **Hrabro ili uspješno dijete?** Hrabro, ali uz protupitanje što znači uspjeh. Za nju je uspjeh da dijete bude **sveto**, a da bi postalo sveto, mora biti hrabro. Zato joj je pitanje „granično“. Voditelj primjećuje da je i za uspjeh potrebna hrabrost, pa je to povezano.

Gošća zaključuje da joj je jedini motiv za djecu da budu sveta. Voditelj dodaje da je to, po njegovu mišljenju, motiv svakog pravog katoličkog roditelja.

magisterium.assessment: U prikazanom ulomku Josipa Nemet izražava sklonost obitelji i djeci, što je u skladu s katoličkim poštovanjem obiteljskog života, ali samo po sebi ne iznosi ni produbljuje određeni nauk. Budući da je odlomak prekinut i sadržava tek dio brzih osobnih pitanja, ne može se na temelju njega procijeniti šira tema podcasta.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje roditeljstva obuhvaća i prihvaćanje djece i njihovu odgojnu odgovornost: roditelji su pozvani prenositi im ljudske vrijednosti i kršćansku vjeru. Ivan Pavao II. opisuje odgoj djece kao dio poslanja obitelji i put posvećenja roditelja, a ne samo kao osobnu životnu sklonost.

magisterium.assessment_en: In the presented excerpt, Josipa Nemet expresses a preference for family and children, which is in accordance with Catholic respect for family life, but does not in itself present or deepen a specific teaching. Since the passage is truncated and contains only a portion of the quick personal questions, the broader theme of the podcast cannot be evaluated on its basis.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of parenthood encompasses both the acceptance of children and the educational responsibility for them: parents are called to transmit human values and the Christian faith to them. John Paul II describes the raising of children as part of the family's mission and a path of sanctification for parents, and not merely as a personal life preference.

sections.subtitle_en: Rapid-fire questions: a house full of children, crocheting, strict rules, and holiness as a measure of success
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks rapid-fire questions, and the guest answers with a smile
sections.content_en:
The host admits that he is sorry to interrupt the conversation and that they could talk for a long time yet. Before the end, however, he asks a few "either-or" rapid-fire questions, warning in advance that some are "tricky". Josipa Nemet's answers reveal her personality:

- **Scientific laboratory or a house full of children?** Without hesitation: a house full of children. The host comments that that was a "sure thing".
- **A basketball game or a quiet dinner with a book?** By now, a quiet dinner with a book. If watching a game, she does not like to watch, but to play. If the choice had been between crocheting and a book, she probably would have chosen crocheting.
- **A parent-teacher meeting or a TV confrontation?** A parent-teacher meeting, because she prefers meeting people in person over anything "disembodied". There, she says, she also has good friends.
- **Homeschooling or a complete reform of schooling?** For her family and the characters of her children, school is better, specifically good schools.
- **Scientific work or public activism?** A woman's great power is in influence, and considering her character, she believes she is more fruitful for society in public activism.
- **Strict rules or complete trust in children?** Strict rules, with the remark that children are happier that way. The host adds: when they know the boundaries.
- **A discussion with an ideological opponent or five hours of children's tantrums?** Neither, and she cannot be objective because a tantrum has never lasted that long for her and she has "her methods" for that. Still, she likes to discuss with ideological opponents, but in a nice way: as a thinking competition, not a debate in which the other is demeaned. In such a conversation, she believes, both grow.
- **A brave or a successful child?** Brave, but with a counter-question of what success means. For her, success is for the child to be **holy**, and to become holy, it must be brave. That is why the question is "borderline" to her. The host observes that courage is also needed for success, so they are connected.

The guest concludes that her only motive for the children is for them to be holy. The host adds that, in his opinion, this is the motive of every true Catholic parent.

sections.subtitle: Zahvala gošći i najava: Dariova krunica među zatvorenicima
sections.screenshot_description: Isječak iz najave sljedeće epizode u kojemu Dario govori o molitvi s krunicom među zatvorenicima
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje Josipi Nemet na gostovanju i svemu što je izrekla te izražava nadu da će njezine riječi mnogima progovoriti. Najavljuje mogućnost još jedne zajedničke epizode jer je ostalo dovoljno materijala. Gošća odgovara da joj je bilo jako ugodno. Emisija se zatvara pozivom gledateljima da lajkaju i pretplate se te da podupru projekt i prate ga na **Patreonu**, gdje je sljedeća epizoda dostupna već danas.

Na samom kraju emitira se isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornik **Dario** govori o iskustvu iz zatvora u kojemu je s krunicom šetao među zatvorenicima, među kojima je katolika bilo malo, a mnogo Arapa i muslimana. Svakog od njih ujutro je javno blagoslivljao svetom vodom, „ne tajno“, i nitko mu nikada nije prigovorio.

Nakon petnaestak dana, prepričava Dario, svaki od zatvorenika počeo ga je moliti da se pomoli za ovo ili ono. Dok su oni kockali za stolom „kao u filmovima“, on je šetao s krunicom i molio za svakoga od njih. Tim molitvama, kaže, pristupao je odgovorno i nikada nije odbio nikoga tko ga je zamolio.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: zahvaljivanje gošći, najava molitve krunice među zatvorenicima i poziv na potporu emisiji sami po sebi ne sadrže teološki sporne tvrdnje. Budući da je Darijevo svjedočanstvo prekinuto i njegov sadržaj nije naveden, taj se dio ne može sadržajno procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica je katolička molitva i može biti sredstvo duhovnog rasta; sveti Josemaría Escrivá opisuje je kao dobru molitvu koja vjerniku pomaže otkrivati njezino značenje. Molitva sa zatvorenicima može biti izraz kršćanske solidarnosti, ali iz ovog sažetka nije moguće zaključiti što je Dario konkretno ispričao niti procijeniti taj sadržaj.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: thanking the guest, announcing the prayer of the Rosary among prisoners, and inviting support for the show do not in themselves contain theologically contentious claims. Since Dario's testimony was cut off and its content is not stated, that part cannot be substantively assessed.

Prayer with prisoners can be an expression of Christian solidarity, but from this summary it is not possible to conclude what Dario specifically recounted nor to assess that content.

sections.subtitle_en: Thanks to the guest and announcement: Dario's Rosary among prisoners
sections.screenshot_description_en: A clip from the preview of the next episode in which Dario speaks about praying with the Rosary among prisoners
sections.content_en:
The host thanks Josipa Nemet for her appearance and everything she stated, and expresses hope that her words will speak to many. He announces the possibility of another joint episode because enough material remained. The guest responds that it was very pleasant for her. The show closes with an invitation to viewers to like and subscribe, and to support the project and follow it on **Patreon**, where the next episode is already available today.

At the very end, a clip from the next episode is aired. The interlocutor **Dario** speaks about an experience from prison where he walked with a Rosary among prisoners, among whom there were few Catholics, and many Arabs and Muslims. Every morning he publicly blessed each of them with holy water, „not secretly”, and no one ever objected to him.

After about fifteen days, Dario recounts, each of the prisoners began asking him to pray for this or that. While they gambled at the table „like in the movies”, he walked with the Rosary and prayed for each of them. He approached these prayers, he says, responsibly and never refused anyone who asked him.
